name: Living-off-the-land and command-line tradecraft
notes: Self-test samples are short, non-functional fragments that use reserved example.invalid hosts. No working payloads are included.

rules.title: Encoded PowerShell command
rules.description: PowerShell was started with a Base64-encoded command, which hides what it runs from casual review and many logs. Common in malware stagers and also used by some management tools.
rules.recommendation: Decode the payload (ConvertFrom-WfxEncodedCommand) and review it; identify the parent process that launched it.

rules.title: PowerShell launched with a hidden window
rules.description: PowerShell was asked to run with no visible window. Legitimate scheduled jobs do this, but so does most malicious PowerShell.
rules.recommendation: Review the full command line and the parent process.

rules.title: PowerShell execution policy bypassed on the command line
rules.description: The execution policy was bypassed for this run. It is a convenience setting rather than a security boundary, but attackers almost always set it.
rules.recommendation: Context only: review together with other findings for the same process.

rules.title: PowerShell downloading content from the web
rules.description: A PowerShell command line fetches content from a URL. Normal for admin scripts; also the first step of most download-and-run attacks.
rules.recommendation: Check the URL's reputation and what was done with the downloaded content.

rules.title: PowerShell download-and-execute cradle
rules.description: Content is downloaded and executed directly in memory in one command — the classic PowerShell stager / 'cradle' pattern. Also how ClickFix-style lures run their payload.
rules.recommendation: Treat as likely malicious: capture the URL, retrieve the content safely for analysis, and trace the parent process.

rules.title: Reference to AMSI internals (possible AMSI bypass)
rules.description: The command references internals of the Antimalware Scan Interface. Outside of security tooling this almost always means an attempt to disable script scanning before running a payload.
rules.recommendation: Treat the process as hostile; review what ran after it.

rules.title: In-memory .NET assembly loading / shellcode API use
rules.description: The command loads .NET code from memory or calls low-level memory APIs — a common way to run tooling without writing it to disk.
rules.recommendation: Capture the script block (4104) or the source of the bytes and analyze it.

rules.title: Obfuscated PowerShell (char-code / concatenation / tick tricks)
rules.description: The command uses string-building tricks that exist mainly to defeat signature matching.
rules.recommendation: Deobfuscate and review; correlate with 4104 script-block logs.

rules.title: Command disables Microsoft Defender or adds an exclusion
rules.description: Defender protection was switched off or an exclusion was added from the command line — very often the step right before a payload is dropped.
rules.recommendation: Check whether this was an approved change; review the exclusion target and what was placed there.

rules.title: Shell history disabled or deleted
rules.description: PowerShell command history was disabled or deleted, which removes a record of what was typed.
rules.recommendation: Recover history from backups / EDR and review the session's other activity.

rules.title: certutil used to download a file
rules.description: certutil.exe is a certificate tool; using it to fetch files from the internet is a well-known living-off-the-land download technique.
rules.recommendation: Find the downloaded file, hash it and check reputation.

rules.title: certutil used to decode a file
rules.description: certutil decoded a Base64/hex file — often used to unpack a payload that was smuggled in as text.
rules.recommendation: Inspect both the input and output files.

rules.title: bitsadmin used to transfer a file
rules.description: BITS was used from the command line to download a file or to run a command when a job completes — a stealthy download/persistence technique.
rules.recommendation: List BITS jobs (bitsadmin /list /allusers /verbose) and inspect the transferred file.

rules.title: mshta executing remote or script content
rules.description: mshta.exe ran HTML Application or script content from a URL, a script URI or a user folder. This is a common initial-access and ClickFix execution path.
rules.recommendation: Retrieve the referenced URL/HTA for analysis and identify what launched mshta.

rules.title: regsvr32 loading a remote scriptlet (Squiblydoo)
rules.description: regsvr32 was told to load a COM scriptlet from a URL or share — a classic application-control bypass.
rules.recommendation: Retrieve the scriptlet for analysis; block outbound access from regsvr32.

rules.title: rundll32 running script or remote content
rules.description: rundll32.exe was used to run script, open a URL handler, or load a DLL from a network share.
rules.recommendation: Review the referenced DLL/URL and the parent process.

rules.title: rundll32 loading a DLL from a user-writable folder
rules.description: rundll32 loaded a DLL from a folder ordinary users can write to — a common way to run a dropped payload.
rules.recommendation: Hash the DLL, check its signature and reputation.

rules.title: msiexec installing a package straight from a URL
rules.description: msiexec installed an MSI directly from the internet — used by several loaders and ClickFix campaigns.
rules.recommendation: Retrieve and analyze the MSI; check for newly installed services/files.

rules.title: MSBuild compiling a project from a user-writable folder
rules.description: MSBuild can run inline C# from a project file; running a project from a user/temp folder outside a build environment is a known application-control bypass.
rules.recommendation: Inspect the project file for inline tasks.

rules.title: InstallUtil used to run code from an assembly
rules.description: InstallUtil.exe ran an assembly's uninstall routine with logging suppressed — a known way to execute code under a signed Microsoft binary.
rules.recommendation: Analyze the referenced assembly.

rules.title: CMSTP installing a connection profile (.inf)
rules.description: cmstp.exe silently installed an INF profile — abused to run commands and bypass UAC.
rules.recommendation: Review the INF file for RunPreSetupCommands.

rules.title: RegAsm/RegSvcs loading a user-path assembly
rules.description: RegAsm/RegSvcs ran registration code from an assembly in a user-writable location.
rules.recommendation: Analyze the assembly.

rules.title: odbcconf used to register a DLL
rules.description: odbcconf.exe registered a DLL or ran a response file — a rarely legitimate proxy-execution technique.
rules.recommendation: Analyze the referenced DLL / .rsp file.

rules.title: WMIC used to start a process (possibly remote)
rules.description: A process was launched through WMI from the command line; with /node this is remote execution (lateral movement).
rules.recommendation: Identify the target host and the launched command.

rules.title: WMIC loading an XSL stylesheet (script execution)
rules.description: WMIC executed script embedded in an XSL stylesheet — an application-control bypass.
rules.recommendation: Retrieve the XSL for analysis.

rules.title: comsvcs.dll MiniDump (LSASS memory dump)
rules.description: The built-in comsvcs.dll MiniDump export was invoked — the most common living-off-the-land way to dump LSASS memory and steal credentials.
rules.recommendation: Assume credential theft: isolate, find the dump file, reset credentials of logged-on accounts.

rules.title: Process-dump tool targeting LSASS
rules.description: A memory-dump utility was pointed at LSASS, which holds credential material.
rules.recommendation: Assume credential theft; locate the dump and contain the host.

rules.title: Mimikatz-style command module
rules.description: Command syntax of the Mimikatz credential-theft tool (or a clone) was observed.
rules.recommendation: Treat the host as compromised; reset exposed credentials and look for lateral movement.

rules.title: Registry hive exported (SAM/SECURITY/SYSTEM)
rules.description: A credential-bearing registry hive was saved to a file — used to extract local password hashes offline.
rules.recommendation: Find and secure the output file; rotate local account passwords.

rules.title: Active Directory database copy (ntdsutil IFM / esentutl / shadow path)
rules.description: The Active Directory database (or a hive) was copied using a technique that bypasses file locks — the step before offline extraction of every domain hash.
rules.recommendation: Treat the domain as potentially compromised; engage incident response.

match: ntdsutil "ac i ntds" ifm "create full C:\t" q q

rules.title: Kerberoasting / AS-REP roasting tooling
rules.description: Tooling that requests service tickets for offline password cracking was used.
rules.recommendation: Identify targeted service accounts and rotate their passwords to long random values.

rules.title: Backups / shadow copies deleted or recovery disabled
rules.description: Shadow copies or backups were deleted, or Windows recovery was disabled — almost always seen right before ransomware encryption.
rules.recommendation: Isolate the host immediately and protect remaining backups.

rules.title: Event log cleared from the command line
rules.description: An event log was cleared, destroying evidence.
rules.recommendation: Recover logs from forwarding/SIEM; find what happened just before.

rules.title: Windows Firewall disabled
rules.description: The host firewall was turned off from the command line.
rules.recommendation: Re-enable it and identify who disabled it.

match: netsh advfirewall set allprofiles state off

rules.title: Registry change used by common UAC bypasses
rules.description: A per-user shell handler that auto-elevating Windows binaries read (fodhelper, eventvwr, …) was modified — the signature of a UAC bypass.
rules.recommendation: Inspect the configured command and remove the key.

rules.title: Scheduled task created to run a script host or user-path program
rules.description: A scheduled task was created that runs an interpreter or a program from a user-writable location — a top persistence technique.
rules.recommendation: Review the task (schtasks /query /tn <name> /xml) and its action.

rules.title: Service created/changed to run an interpreter or user-path binary
rules.description: A Windows service was created or reconfigured to run a shell command or a binary from a user-writable path — used for persistence and remote execution.
rules.recommendation: Inspect the service and its binary; remove if not legitimate.

rules.title: Run key written from the command line
rules.description: An autostart Run key was added from the command line.
rules.recommendation: Review the value and the program it starts.

rules.title: Image File Execution Options debugger / SilentProcessExit set
rules.description: An IFEO debugger or SilentProcessExit monitor was configured, which hijacks a program's launch.
rules.recommendation: Inspect and remove the value; check the referenced binary.

match: reg add "HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Image File Execution Options\sethc.exe" /v Debugger /d cmd.exe

rules.title: Local account created from the command line
rules.description: A local user account was created from the command line — a common way for intruders to keep access.
rules.recommendation: Confirm the account is authorized; disable it if not.

rules.title: Account added to a privileged group
rules.description: An account was added to an administrative or remote-access group.
rules.recommendation: Confirm the change was authorized; review the account's activity.

rules.title: netsh port forwarding configured
rules.description: A port proxy was configured, turning this host into a relay — used to pivot into internal networks.
rules.recommendation: List rules (netsh interface portproxy show all) and remove unauthorized ones.

match: netsh interface portproxy add v4tov4 listenport=8443 connectaddress=10.0.0.5 connectport=3389

rules.title: SSH / plink reverse tunnel
rules.description: An SSH reverse tunnel exposes a local port (often RDP) to a remote host — a common way to get persistent inbound access.
rules.recommendation: Identify the remote endpoint and the exposed port.

rules.title: RDP enabled or opened in the firewall
rules.description: Remote Desktop was enabled or allowed through the firewall from the command line.
rules.recommendation: Confirm this was intended.

rules.title: Active Directory reconnaissance tooling
rules.description: Commands that enumerate domain trusts, admins or the AD graph were run — typical early ransomware-operator activity.
rules.recommendation: Correlate with the user and host; check for follow-on lateral movement.

rules.title: curl download followed by execution
rules.description: A file was downloaded with curl and immediately executed — common in ClickFix and loader one-liners.
rules.recommendation: Retrieve the file for analysis and identify the lure that produced the command.

rules.title: Command carrying a fake-CAPTCHA / 'verify you are human' lure (ClickFix)
rules.description: The command line contains social-engineering text used by ClickFix / fake-CAPTCHA lures, which trick users into pasting a command into the Run dialog or a terminal.
rules.recommendation: Treat as malicious: identify the website that delivered the lure and analyze what the command fetched.

match: powershell -w h -c "Write-Output x" # I am not a robot - Verification ID 4471

rules.title: Windows Script Host running a script from a user folder
rules.description: wscript/cscript ran a script from a user-writable location — the typical execution of a malicious email or download attachment.
rules.recommendation: Retrieve the script and analyze it.

rules.title: Defender's MpCmdRun used to download a file
rules.description: MpCmdRun.exe was abused as a downloader.
rules.recommendation: Retrieve the downloaded file for analysis.
